title: Musical Composition Collection Map and Coverage Review
scope: Baseline reconciliation of 15 proposed collections and 60 candidates with 49 songwriting sources. Coverage counts refer to 29 October 2026. Dated integration annotations record later curriculum and player work without silently treating formal-model explanations as new dedicated pattern articles. See curriculum_integration_review for the current implementation.

coverage_definitions.dedicated: An existing pattern has the same central creative situation and reusable move. Domain framing or demonstrations may still need work.
coverage_definitions.embedded: An explicit developed passage or concrete seed exists within a broader article; this is not a dedicated pattern.
coverage_definitions.gap: No developed treatment of this candidate exists; incidental mentions and related foundations are recorded without counting as coverage.

process_scope: Methods can have process scope instead of being forced into the sound-to-piece hierarchy. Musical levels express the material acted upon, not technical difficulty, musical pitch-scale type, or workflow duration.

families.title: Musical Relationships and Development
families.question: How can material interact and grow?

families.title: Creative Methods and Approaches
families.question: How can I discover, develop, and finish an approach?

collections.title: Melody & Phrasing
collections.use_when: A line lacks direction, punctuation, or a recognizable focal feature.
collections.boundary: Shape the identity and articulation of a single musical line.

collections.title: Harmony & Tonality
collections.use_when: Pitches and chords need a clear relationship, color, or destination.
collections.boundary: Organize pitch collections, centers, simultaneous notes, and harmonic movement.

collections.title: Rhythm & Groove
collections.use_when: A recurring pulse or the events around it need more purposeful movement.
collections.boundary: Shape pulse, grouping, subdivision, timing, and rhythmic reference.

collections.title: Timbre & Sound Design
collections.use_when: The character of the sounds should become compositional material.
collections.boundary: Choose and transform the identity of sounds, including sources beyond pitched instruments.

collections.title: Texture & Layering
collections.use_when: Simultaneous parts compete, obscure one another, or need complementary roles.
collections.boundary: Organize which layers coexist and what each contributes.

collections.title: Space & Atmosphere
collections.use_when: The apparent distance, placement, or acoustic continuity of sounds should shape the music.
collections.boundary: Compose perceived depth, spatial position, motion, and reverberant relationships.

collections.title: Dynamics & Gesture
collections.use_when: A sound or phrase needs a more purposeful attack, continuation, release, or emphasis.
collections.boundary: Shape the physical and temporal behavior of sounds and gestures.

collections.title: Motifs & Thematic Development
collections.use_when: An idea needs recognizable continuation, variation, or transformation.
collections.boundary: Develop relationships within and between recognizable units of material.

collections.title: Counterpoint & Voice Interaction
collections.use_when: A second line needs its own musical identity while belonging with the first.
collections.boundary: Combine independently meaningful melodic lines; distinguish this from chord voicing.

collections.title: Tension, Release & Musical Drama
collections.use_when: A passage needs expectation, a consequential arrival, or a convincing trajectory.
collections.boundary: Plan the experience of preparation, intensification, withholding, and release.

collections.title: Musical Form & Structure
collections.use_when: Strong local ideas need a convincing larger relationship of return and change.
collections.boundary: Organize larger spans and the overall experience of a piece.

collections.title: Transitions & Endings
collections.use_when: A boundary feels pasted together or an ending does not complete the intended experience.
collections.boundary: Shape entrances, joins, departures, and final gestures.

collections.title: Sampling & Sound Manipulation
collections.use_when: Existing audio should become new compositional material through reuse or transformation.
collections.boundary: Work with recorded audio as material, including loops and resampling.

collections.title: Creative Processes & Constraints
collections.use_when: A habitual starting point, stalled process, or unfinished draft prevents progress.
collections.boundary: Choose generative methods, constraints, revision moves, and ways to finish.

collections.title: Songwriting & Music–Text Relationships
collections.use_when: Words, speaker, musical emphasis, and sectional meaning need to work together.
collections.boundary: Compose the relationship between language and music, preserving song-specific craft.

integration_review.decision: Explain within the canonical form-choice article and connect to development/return techniques. A separate technique article is not justified by a formal label alone. Full model-specific guided demonstration remains future work.

overlap_decisions.decision: Keep the timed-silence move in Rhythm & Groove. Acoustic spaciousness belongs in Space & Atmosphere only when perceived depth or spatial relationships, rather than rests, are the mechanism.

Treat layered entry as one implementation of accumulation unless a separate problem and boundary justify a pattern. Foreground/background and interlocking layers retain their distinct simultaneous-role decisions.
Use one canonical Textural Subtraction entry in Texture & Layering; link its dramatic release uses to Musical Drama.
Keep Reserve the Peak as a named facet initially. Single-line contour stays in Melody; whole-piece contrast planning stays in Musical Drama.

Reuse the existing exact sequence and fragment examples. Separate a technique only if it needs a genuinely distinct article. Check the historical developing-variation term before equating it with any selective variation.
Map smooth chord voice leading to Harmony, bass roles to Texture, and independent melodic-line construction to Counterpoint. Related material is preparation, not complete counterpoint coverage.
Keep the introductory arpeggio/block example in the chord foundation. A moving accompaniment through a progression is a distinct compositional application with one canonical home in Harmony.
Selecting a sound world is existing palette coverage. Altering source identity and reusing recorded material need their own decisions; changing an instrument preset does not cover all three.
An ostinato is the recurring anchor, strategic repetition chooses the role of returns, and phasing changes relative alignment. Do not count a loop switch as all three techniques.
An ending passage can supply a coda seed, but the label alone does not teach its function. AABA coverage does not satisfy the proposed ABA pattern.
Define the shared collection by musical continuity and change. A continuous timbral process does not necessarily introduce new thematic sections in the same way as a through-composed song.
Store one canonical collection per pattern and several meaningful musical levels when appropriate. Learning paths and secondary cross-references may point to it without duplicating the article.

learning_journey.title: Discover musical possibilities
learning_journey.focus: Introduce sound, rhythm, melody, texture, space, process, and language as legitimate starting points.
guides: Eight Ways to Start a Composition
learning_journey.notes: These guide titles are proposals, not newly authored patterns or a replacement for existing introductory articles.

learning_journey.title: Create a first idea
learning_journey.notes: Offer a sound-led route and the existing five-pattern note foundation as equal optional entrances; do not require a theory course first.

learning_journey.title: Complete the piece
learning_journey.notes: Completing a miniature is also an early option; phase order is guidance rather than a prerequisite gate.

first_development_shortlist.reason: Give sound-led beginners a concrete attack/sustain/release relationship before adding many synthesis controls.
Make evolving sound an equal compositional starting point alongside the existing note foundations.
Open the otherwise unrepresented space collection with a small, audible distance comparison.
Establish recorded material as something a composer can develop, beyond a repeating note figure.
Add the clearest missing technique from the user shortlist and distinguish it from ordinary interlocking.
Create the first explicit two-independent-line pattern before teaching stricter counterpoint methods.
Extend the existing chord comparison into a useful moving-accompaniment decision.
Expose an already precise transformation that can be demonstrated with the existing note scheduler.

review_method: Inventory all 49 current chapter titles, situations, responses, boundaries, and section headings; inspect relevant manuscript passages for candidate coverage and overlap decisions. Check exact source-heading references and inspect current player/editor code and bindings. Coverage judgments, musical levels, and proposed homes are editorial inferences. This review does not audition recordings or select new repertoire.

handoff_reconciliation.decision: A layer entrance can support accumulation or replace another role. Keep it as an application until a distinct creative problem justifies a separate pattern.

integration_review.disposition: Named technique and original A/B implemented within Shape Energy over Time; retain one canonical home.

handoff_reconciliation.decision: Timed rests and empty attacks belong with Strategic Silence. Perceived spatial openness belongs with Space & Atmosphere only when acoustic placement or depth is the mechanism.
An abrupt dynamic change is a gesture variant; a change of sectional role links to Sectional Contrast. Do not add a generic duplicate contrast entry.
Keep as a concrete creative-process constraint rather than requiring a separate article with the same starting-point decision.
The existing entrance pattern already covers pickups and anticipation. Preserve their distinctions: a pickup is not automatically the same thing as syncopation.
Use one canonical subtraction pattern and link its release function to Musical Drama.
Connect selective variation to the existing energy pattern’s changed successive returns. Keep the returning section in its whole-piece context.
The formal compositional technique is not developed by calling a phrase a musical sentence. Keep as an optional Form & Structure candidate at phrase level, outside the current 60-candidate shortlist.
